title: The right panel shows the binder you picked
summary: The status page's main panel still groups every binder under Now, Next and Later, so it renders all of them at once with empty group headings above and below. The design has no grouping there at all: the map on the left picks a binder and the panel on the right is that binder's detail. This binder makes the page work that way and closes the six differences the last design comparison left open.
motivation:
The previous binder removed the phase spine and was read as having removed the phase model with it — the grouping survived, and the comparison that caught it could not fix it without changing how the panel is driven.

Every open finding the 2026-08-18 run recorded is closed by an item here, and the mapping is written down so a gap shows as an absence rather than being discovered at the gate. Finding 1, the phase grouping, is panel-is-one-binder; its box-level sub-check is drill-in-fidelity-gate's second assertion, deliberately counted apart from the delivery frame because reading the two together is how the previous run nearly cleared the defect; its corner sub-finding already landed in 81f77c2, and the general rule it asks for — does any opaque last child sit square inside a rounded container — is progress-track-pill's. Finding 2, the binder summary, and finding 4, the three smaller type gaps with the slug's chip and icon, are both binder-head-type-scale. Finding 3, the square-ended progress track, is progress-track-pill. Finding 5, the inverted card ground, is card-ground-and-tint-base. Finding 6, the live-page controls, is live-controls-recorded. Four items answer to no finding: rail-is-the-selector is the mechanism the panel item needs, alarm-motion-softens and rail-halt-badge come from the fact-table gaps, and fact-to-assertion-trace is the recurrence guard — all four are named in scope.included rather than inherited from the run.

design_facts.stack: Python stdlib http.server + vendored Vue 3 SPA, shipped as a Claude Code / Codex plugin skill

isolation_params: --port <n> — the loopback port the server binds. 8700 is pinned rather than the script's own default 8765, because the multi-repo hub derives its port as 8765 + uid % 1000 (serve_status.py:230-238) and collides with the default outright on a uid-1000 host; --ensure then respawns the hub and the command fails with Errno 98. A wave run may substitute its own port here

--root <dir> — pass only the pinned value docs/designs/fixtures/watch-fidelity-state; a wave must not substitute its own. It points the page at the committed fixture the fidelity runbook names (docs/conventions/watch-design-fidelity.md:17), which is what makes the shape the page derives — one binder, one wave, one card — fixed across runs. A wave that injects its own --root un-pins the fixture and the comparison stops being repeatable

KARTA_WATCH_STATE_DIR — overrides the multi-repo hub's own store directory (state.json, state.lock, a token file). Worth setting so a run never touches the real per-user store; it carries no binder or wave state and cannot point the page at a fixture

component_map.implementation: the page's rail card control is today an <a :href="'#binder-' + c.slug"> (serve_status.py:3824) whose only effect is a scroll jump, because the page renders every binder at once. It becomes a button that sets the selected slug. The rail's four groups, its gutter, its dots and its Delivered toggle are untouched — the design groups its map the same way and this item is about the control, not the grouping

component_map.design: the picked card is marked twice over: border:2px solid var(--now) with outline:2px solid var(--now-deep) at outline-offset:3px on the card (export 186), and background:var(--now-soft) on the button inside it (export 187). The other four carry a 1px var(--line) border, no outline, and a transparent button that only tints on hover (export 163, 164)
component_map.implementation: a selected modifier on the existing .rail__pick / card structure carrying those two treatments. The page already has a .rail__pick--now modifier bound to c.now (serve_status.py:3824, 1653) — that one says 'this binder is in flight', which is a different claim from 'this is the one you are looking at'. Both can be true of one card and neither implies the other, so selection gets its own modifier rather than borrowing that one. The design settles nothing about which mark is which, because its ringed card is also its only in-flight card. This binder decides it: the ring and the 2px border are SELECTION's mark, and in flight keeps the marks the design's own legend names for it — the breathing gutter dot, the sole progress bar, the --now-deep figure and its Now grouping. So the two states stay readable on one screen when they land on different cards

contract.exposes: a selected-binder slug held in the app's data, the method that sets it, and a data-kw-rail-selected hook on the picked card. The default selection is derived, never typed: the in-flight binder if the state has one, else the first binder the rail's own group order yields — the same order railGroupsOf already computes (serve_status.py:3118-3160), so the map and the default can never disagree.
contract.consumes: the binder list already in the state feed, and railGroupsOf's existing classification. No new server field, no new git call.
contract.regression_risk: the control changes element type, so anything that depended on it being a link breaks: the href-driven scroll jump, and .binder's scroll-margin-top (serve_status.py:1800) which exists only to land that jump below the sticky header. Both are this item's to account for — the jump target disappears in the next item, so this item must not leave a dead scroll-margin rule behind it either. Two checks read that rule and fail on the true render once it is gone: _BAR_DERIVED (serve_status.py:8434), which proves all four bar-derived offsets move when the bar height changes, and _c_wave_step_sticky (serve_status.py:9973). Nothing replaces the offset — the jump it existed for is gone — so both must be re-stated to cover the three offsets that remain, not re-pointed at a substitute. Five prose statements still say four offsets hang off the bar height and go false with the fourth gone: serve_status.py:1176-1181, 2134-2139, 8430 and 8499-8503, plus selftest_behaviours.txt:297 — the committed anchor, already in this item's touches. Nothing in the suite reads a comment, so all five are corrected by hand in the same commit or they drift silently.
contract.preserves: the rail's four groups, the Delivered toggle and its derived label, the gutter dots and stems, and the legend. A binder that is in flight still reads as in flight whether or not it is the selected one. The map header's hint keeps saying what it says today — the wording already names picking rather than jumping (RAIL_HINT, serve_status.py:2458) and the count is already derived (railHint(), serve_status.py:3446-3448), both guarded with a negative control by design-wording-lands-where-the-design-puts-it (serve_status.py:10794). The assertion below is a regression guard on work already done, not a change this item makes, and it is listed here so the traceability rule is satisfied rather than sidestepped.

contract.regression_risk: two registered behaviours hook on data-kw-phase — phase-timeline-groups (serve_status.py:11383) and no-phase-spine-beside-the-panel (serve_status.py:11463) — and both are named in selftest_behaviours.txt, which validate_plugin.py enforces as a floor. The two are NOT the same move. phase-timeline-groups asserts the grouping's shape and is genuinely retired. no-phase-spine-beside-the-panel reads what a spine is MADE OF — position, background, background-color, width, plus an icon ban (serve_status.py:11469-11494) — over everything between the panel start tag and the first binder, and its own docstring says a spine rebuilt under a different class name still fails it. That region survives this item (panel__head and panel__note remain), so the check is re-keyed onto the surviving chrome rather than retired; hook reuse is existing precedent (serve_status.py:11498, 11542). Removing a hook without retiring or re-keying through that anchor fails the build; deleting the names quietly is the move the anchor exists to stop. Each retirement must be replaced by a behaviour making the stronger claim, not merely dropped. A third check breaks and is not about data-kw-phase at all: MAIN_TO_CARD_LEVELS = 6 (serve_status.py:1166) is read by _c_card_sits_one_level_shallower (serve_status.py:11641), anchored as a-card-sits-one-level-shallower. Deleting div.phase and div.phase__binders takes the measured depth from 6 to 4 and the check returns False. The constant is the answer this item changes — re-state it to 4 with its comment rewritten to say what the two removed levels were; do NOT reintroduce a wrapper to keep the number at 6, which is the cheap fix a red check invites. frame-inset-comes-from-named-steps (anchor line 68) also carries two break mutators keyed on .phase and .phase__binders, which go vacuous once those selectors are gone; re-key them onto nodes that still exist rather than leaving mutators that can never fire.
contract.preserves: the delivery frame and what it carries — which repository this watch is of and how many binders it holds — booked as intended difference 3 in the fidelity record. The rail keeps its four groups and its Delivered toggle; the collapse control on the binder panel keeps working.

work_items.title: Make a recorded design fact prove it is checked
work_items.summary: Add a check that every design fact a binder records is traced to an assertion that depends on it, or is marked untraced with a reason.

contract.exposes: a stdlib-only check, in the house pattern (argparse, a --self-test mode printing [PASS]/[FAIL] lines), that reads a binder's design fact table and requires every fact to carry either a trace naming the work item and the assertion that depends on it, or an explicit untraced reason. The grammar is pinned here so the check and its subject cannot disagree: a trace is '<item-id>:<0-based assertion index>', and the table lives at token_manifest.design_fact_table — not under design_facts, which is additionalProperties:false in the schema and could never hold one. The sweep is non-recursive .karta/binders/*.json: an archived binder is unwritable by the immutability guard, so a trace rule there would be unsatisfiable by construction. Wired into the repo's floor so it runs unprompted.
contract.consumes: the binder JSON only. It reads no git state and starts no server.
contract.regression_risk: a binder with no design fact table must pass untouched — the check applies to binders that record facts, and turning it into a requirement that every binder record facts would be a wider rule than the defect calls for. A trace that names an item id or an assertion that does not exist has to fail; a trace that names them but where the assertion does not actually depend on the fact cannot be caught by a script, and the check must say so rather than implying it proves more than it does.
contract.preserves: the existing binder schema for every binder that records no facts, and the existing validator's behaviour on all of them.

assertions: a fact table where every fact carries a trace naming a real work item passes
a fact table with one untraced fact fails, and the failure names that fact
a trace naming a work item id that does not exist in the binder fails, and so does one naming an assertion index the item does not have
a fact carrying an explicit untraced reason passes, and the reason is echoed in the check's output so it is visible rather than silent
a binder with no design fact table passes untouched — the fixture for this includes a real binder from this repo that records none
the check's own limit is stated in its output or its usage text: it proves a fact NAMES an assertion, never that the assertion depends on the fact
the check runs as part of the repo's floor, so a fact table added later cannot go untraced without failing the build
this binder's own fact table passes the check

The oracle type is 'unit' on purpose, and reverting it to 'visual' would break this item. karta-build routes a visual oracle to karta-validate for acceptance (karta-build/SKILL.md:348), and karta-validate's comparison worker is handed only the capture JSON — 'it has not seen the app code, design files, or pipeline state' (karta-validate/SKILL.md:118). None of that is in a capture JSON. Worse, karta-validate's Phase 1 mandatorily serves the design through serve_design.py, which hard-roots at the design file's own parent (karta-validate/scripts/serve_design.py:73, no root flag) — the exact path assertion 0 forbids, because it 404s all eight faces and the mascot and poisons the px-level type readings. Under 'unit' the browser run still happens exactly as the runbook describes — the wave env_contract serves the page at 127.0.0.1:8700 and the design opens over file:// — and karta-verify dispositions all nine assertions against the diff, which is where the run's evidence lands.

the number of box levels between the main panel and the binder card is counted and reported, and it equals the design's — checked apart from the delivery frame, because reading the two together is exactly how the previous run nearly cleared this defect
each of the six open findings the 2026-08-18 run recorded is re-checked by name and reported as fixed or still open, so a finding cannot be closed by silence

the gate lists every waiver in this binder and records, for each, the assertion of this run that discharged it or — where the pinned view could not show the waived facet — names it as not observable in this run and points at the unit assertion in the waiving item that proves what can be proven instead. A waiver left off the list is a failure of this item; a waiver honestly recorded as unobservable is not
the run names what the pinned fixture could not show — the halt badge, the in-flight ring and any part-filled progress bar — and does not record a verdict on any of them

the run's verdict is derived from what it observed and is recorded even when it is a fail; a difference found that is on neither closed list is written down as an open finding rather than promoted into the intended list
the recorded run states which of its claims came from a screenshot and which from computed values, so a later reader can tell what was seen from what was measured

the header bar's rendered height is measured in the browser and recorded beside the claim the constant's own comment makes (serve_status.py:1168-1174) and the same claim restated as arithmetic in _c_bar_height_named_once's docstring (serve_status.py:8506, which a search for '71' will never reach). If measurement and comment disagree, BOTH statements are rewritten to say what the design renders and what this page renders — the design carries the border on a separate outer element (export 111-112) while this page collapses both onto one border-box element, so the two numbers can legitimately differ and simply editing 71 to 70 would leave the sentence self-contradicting

the readings behind the panel click, and behind one work-item card's disclosure, are taken and reported — the fixture binder derives as next and the page opens only the current binder's panel at rest (serve_status.py:3492), so the work-item cards are absent from the DOM until clicked. The run names which waived item each card-level reading pays; a run that never opens the panel leaves those waivers unpaid while satisfying every other assertion here

signals: scope of impact — serve_status.py is edited by eight of this binder's ten items, so each one is serialized behind the others
not-computed:sensitive — this repo configures no sensitive-path convention, so that signal could not be evaluated
capability or resource escalation — this item serves the page and drives a browser, which no deterministic check in this repo does
